# Wave repair: task 1 convergence exception, then escalation

## 1. Decision on the current re-review

The observed trajectory line is `TRAJECTORY: CONVERGING (3 -> 1, max severity Moderate)`.

- The test is whether the line contains `max severity Critical`. It does not, because the remaining maximum is `Moderate`.
- `failed[1] == 2` was reached by a `CONVERGING` re-review, and `converged[1]` is unset.
- So the convergence exception applies:
  - set `converged[1]`
  - run **one extra ordinary repair** (no `model:`)
  - re-review afterward

If the line had read `max severity Critical`, there would be no exception. The flow would go straight to the escalated round in §3.

Other state:
- Task 1 stays `in_progress`, and task 2 is untouched.
- The round cap is still in force: no more than `4 + N` re-reviews in this wave.
- I use a bounded direct read (`limit: 300`) of the FIX_FIRST report only if structured `touchedTasks` and findings do not already attribute the finding to task 1.

## 2. Extra ordinary repair for task 1 (isolated wave)

### 2a. Repair-base snapshot

```bash
RP_ROOT='/workspace/project'
RP_BASE='1111111111111111111111111111111111111111'
RP_DIR=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
RP_TREE="$RP_DIR/tree"
git -C "$RP_ROOT" add -A || exit 1
git -C "$RP_ROOT" diff --binary --cached "$RP_BASE" > "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" || exit 1
git -C "$RP_ROOT" worktree add --detach "$RP_TREE" "$RP_BASE" || exit 1
if [ -s "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" ]; then git -C "$RP_TREE" apply --index "$RP_DIR/integrated.patch" || exit 1; fi
git -C "$RP_TREE" -c user.name=gauntlet -c user.email=gauntlet@local commit -q --allow-empty -m "wave integrated snapshot" || exit 1
printf 'repair-base: %s %s\n' "$RP_TREE" "$(git -C "$RP_TREE" rev-parse HEAD)"
```

### 2b. Repair implementer carrier

This is foreground, file-only and schema-bound. It has no `context: "fresh"` and no `model:`.

```ts
subagent({ async: false, cwd: "<RP_TREE printed above>",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "implementer", as: "impl_1",
      outputSchema: IMPLEMENTER_STATUS_SCHEMA,
      output: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-repair<k>-task1.md", outputMode: "file-only",
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/feature.md; anchor: ### Task 1:; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/feature.md; Leg: <owning leg>; Rules: <task 1 Rules> + <leg> Rules from home ## Legs, resolved in the owning checkout; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: <task 1 manifest tests verbatim, or none>.\nFix the FIX_FIRST findings attributed to task 1.\n## Previous review report (re-review trigger)\n<path of the CONVERGING FIX_FIRST report>\nRead the saved report yourself. pi-cohort saves your final report; do not write it yourself." }
  ], worktree: true, concurrency: 4,
     stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED", "NEEDS_CONTEXT", "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS"] } }]
})
```

### 2c. Integrate the delta

Run this only after a `DONE` or `DONE_WITH_CONCERNS` result arrives. The delta is the `Artifacts:` patch.

```bash
git -C '/workspace/project' apply --index '<Artifacts dir>/worktree-diffs/step-0/task-0-implementer.patch'
```

- Then print: `wave <w> repair <k> task 1 <status> report <path> delta <path> applied <yes|no>`
- Then run:

```bash
git -C '/workspace/project' worktree remove --force '<RP_TREE>'
```

- If the apply fails, that counts as a failed attempt and triggers the rebuild.

### 2d. Record the tree, check emptiness, run the gate

Record the tree first:

```bash
FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
FD_STATUS=$?
rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"
```

Then check emptiness and run the gate:

```bash
git -C '/workspace/project' add -A
git -C '/workspace/project' diff --stat '<prior review tree>' '<tree just printed>'
(cd '/workspace/project' && <task 1 manifest test command>) > '<REPORT_DIR>/gate-<i>.log' 2>&1; echo "wave <w> gate <i> exit $?"
```

- An empty `--stat` is +1 failed attempt with no re-review. It sends "your fix changed no tracked file".
- A red gate means a repair from the gate log, not a review.

### 2e. Re-review carrier

Dispatch this only when the gate is green.

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "wave-reviewer", output: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-review<k+1>.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: WAVE_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/feature.md; anchors: ### Task 1:, ### Task 2:; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/feature.md; Leg: <owning leg>; Rules: <combined task/leg Rules, resolved in the owning checkout>; BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111; HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: <wave union of manifest tests>\n## Previous review report (re-review trigger)\n<path of the CONVERGING FIX_FIRST report>\n## Fix delta\ntree-before: <prior review tree>\ntree-after: <tree recorded in 2d>\nRun git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <tree-before> <tree-after> yourself. Apply the trajectory block." }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["FIX_FIRST", "REJECT"] } }]
})
```

Then print: `wave <w> review <k+1> verdict <value> report <path> tree <sha>`

## 3. The next re-review is FIX_FIRST again (CONVERGING)

- The convergence exception is already spent. A further `FIX_FIRST` escalates whatever the trajectory says, so the Critical comparison no longer matters.
- This brings `failed[1]` above 2 with `escalated[1]` unset, so I set `escalated[1]`.

Print `escalated round for task 1 after 2 failed attempts`, then call:

```ts
gauntlet_setting({ key: "escalationLoop" })
```

If `implModel` is undefined or the tool is unavailable, I stop with a note per stop-note.md.

Otherwise:
1. Re-run the §2a repair-base block exactly as written.
2. Dispatch the same payload with only the `model:` added:

```ts
subagent({ async: false, cwd: "<new RP_TREE>", model: "<implModel verbatim>",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "implementer", as: "impl_1",
      outputSchema: IMPLEMENTER_STATUS_SCHEMA,
      output: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-repair<k+1>-task1.md", outputMode: "file-only",
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/feature.md; anchor: ### Task 1:; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/feature.md; Leg: <owning leg>; Rules: <task 1 Rules> + <leg> Rules from home ## Legs, resolved in the owning checkout; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: <task 1 manifest tests verbatim, or none>.\n## Previous review report (re-review trigger)\n<path of the latest FIX_FIRST report>\nRead the saved report yourself. pi-cohort saves your final report; do not write it yourself." }
  ], worktree: true, concurrency: 4,
     stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED", "NEEDS_CONTEXT", "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS"] } }]
})
```

After that, steps 2c–2e repeat as written: apply, remove the worktree, record the tree, check `--stat`, run the gate and re-review.

## Where I stop

I stop here, at the boundary, awaiting the escalated round's terminal result.

- If it fails, the next step is a funded round, if the task's grant ledger has one left. Otherwise it is a stop note with the `budget:` line.
- I am not reporting any verdict, SHA, path or outcome that was not observed.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After gets the sequencing right: at failed[1]==2 with a CONVERGING line that lacks `max severity Critical` and `converged[1]` unset it sets `converged[1]`, runs exactly one extra ordinary repair, states that a Critical line would skip straight to escalation, and treats the following FIX_FIRST as escalating regardless of trajectory. Before failed the same fact not because of wording but because it shifted the decision one round late — it treated the review at failed[1]==2 as 'ordinary budget, exception not used yet', dispatched a fix, and only then applied the Critical test and granted the exception on the next FIX_FIRST (which by the protocol should have escalated whatever the trajectory), effectively permitting two post-limit repairs. The one thing After leaves implicit is the fourth clause: it never says what happens when `TRAJECTORY:` is missing or malformed (Before explicitly said 'I do not re-dispatch just to obtain the line' and treated missing/malformed like STAGNANT/DIVERGING). To keep that clause unambiguous while retaining the new transition-table framing, add one bullet to §1 along the lines of 'a missing or malformed TRAJECTORY: line counts as a failed attempt and escalates on the current tree; I do not re-dispatch the reviewer merely to obtain the line', so the folded table covers the missing-trajectory row as well as the Critical and spent-exception rows.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Both outputs keep the convergence-exception protocol intact: each permits exactly one ordinary repair only when the re-review is FIX_FIRST CONVERGING with non-Critical max severity and converged[1] unset, each records converged[1] when consuming it, each escalates on the next FIX_FIRST regardless of continued convergence, each escalates immediately on Critical with no exception, and neither redispatches a review merely to obtain a missing TRAJECTORY line. After additionally delivers the Change (committed repair-base snapshot, delta-only apply, single wave-reviewer re-review, escalation on the current integrated tree with a runtime-resolved model), so no fact moved. One small wording inconsistency in After worth tightening: the transition table says to 'increment the attributed failure count' on the second FIX_FIRST, but the escalation banner then reads 'after 2 failed attempts' — either state the incremented count (3) or drop the increment sentence so the two lines agree; this does not break the fact but a careful reader may trip on it.
